experiment.claim: README.md 'Target specification (ratified -- see DR-005, issue #1)' row 'Supply' (3.3 V +/-10%) read as an output-shift requirement, checked against the only bound the ratified spec implies without inventing a number: the supply-induced shift must fit inside the entire +/-2% untrimmed output-accuracy window (48 mV p-p on 1.20 V). NECESSARY, not sufficient -- a real budget gives line regulation a fraction of that window. Setting a dedicated line-regulation line item remains a future spec pass's call; these numbers are its input.
experiment.title: Line regulation: untrimmed output shift across the full 3.3 V +/-10% supply range

spread_checks.note: Primary corner-liveness guard for this bench: VREF at the nominal supply must move by at least 5 mV across the 15-point process/temperature matrix. It spans ~33 mV (1.1747 V at the hot corners to 1.2082 V at the cold ones), so this is a wide-margin assertion that the .lib corner include and .temp really are reaching the simulator. It is placed on VREF rather than on the line shift because VREF is the quantity with a large, well-understood corner dependence; the line shift is a second-order effect measured in tens of microvolts and is a poor liveness signal.

Secondary guard: the supply-induced shift must itself move by at least 5 uV across the matrix. RE-SCALED from the original 0.05 mV. That threshold was set against the first run of this bench, whose 0.11 .. 1.27 mV readings turned out to be the DC solver's convergence noise floor rather than the circuit (see the tolerance note below). With the noise removed the real quantity is 0.0074 .. 0.030 mV, so a 0.05 mV spread requirement can never be met and the guard fires on every run -- as it did on record 20260803-115354-7759435, which is committed as a failing record. The new threshold is scaled to the resolved magnitude and still leaves ~4.5x margin on the observed 0.023 mV spread, while sitting three orders of magnitude above the noise floor at these tolerances. Note what did NOT change: the pass window on the measurement itself (24 mV) is untouched -- no spec bound was moved to make anything pass, only a harness self-check that had been calibrated against a number now known to be an artifact.
